title: Ballot Problem OQ-01-OQ-02-OQ-02: LGV Determinant for Path Orderings
description: Formalizes the MacMahon-LGV product formula for the probability that ballot lead ordering is maintained throughout counting: P = ∏_{i<j} (aᵢ - aⱼ)/(aᵢ + aⱼ). Proves the 2-candidate case from Mathlib's ballot theorem, concrete numerical verifications for small cases, monotonicity of ballot ratio, and the 2×2 determinant structure. 2 axioms for the 3-candidate LGV extension. 15 theorems.

overview.historicalContext: MacMahon (1915) found the product formula via non-intersecting lattice paths (LGV lemma).
overview.problemStatement: Prove the ordering probability formula via Lindström-Gessel-Viennot.
overview.proofStrategy: 2-candidate case from Mathlib ballot theorem; concrete verifications for (3,1), (4,2), (4,2,1), (5,3,1); 2 axioms for 3-candidate LGV.
keyInsights: **orderingProbability_two**: Classical ballot theorem for 2-candidate ordering probability
